extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in Indian media and politics (journalists, researchers, general public)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and indicators for recognizing 'Godi media' — Indian print/TV outlets perceived as pro-government or propagandistic. Useful for evaluating whether a news outlet or journalist functions as a mouthpiece of the ruling party or spreads disinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — pro-government biased media ('Godi media')
rubrics_metrics.description: A term coined to describe biased Indian print and TV news media which has openly supported the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party government since 2014; idiomatically 'lapdog media' or 'media sitting on lap'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a label for television and other media perceived as 'mouthpieces of the ruling party' (i.e., the BJP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open support for the ruling party / functioning as a 'mouthpiece'
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlets that openly support the ruling BJP government and act as mouthpieces of the ruling party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for editorial line, repeated praise, uncritical coverage of government initiatives, and systematic downplaying of criticism or opposition voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing fake news and inflammatory, often untrue stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Detractors allege Godi media publishes fake news and inflammatory stories which are often untrue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes amplification of false claims, misleading framing, or reliance on unreliable sources; these practices are cited as evidence of abandoning honest journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working in interest of Hindutva, Sangh Parivar, corporate or elite sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that serves the ideological aims of Hindutva or the Sangh Parivar, or the business/political interests of corporate and elite sources rather than public-interest journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess source selection, recurring narratives, and alignment with partisan ideological talking points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial reorganisation and personnel changes favoring pro-government anchors
rubrics_metrics.description: Taming of media via reorganisation of editorial authority: removal of senior editors deemed 'left-wing' and development of new channels/anchors devoted to the BJP and Modi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators include abrupt leadership changes, hiring patterns that favor partisan presenters, and programming shifts toward pro-government commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial incentives / dependence on state and party advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Large state and party advertising budgets give governments considerable control over media companies; heavy government ad-spend is an incentive for favorable coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine revenue sources, government advertising volumes (e.g., central government ad spend statistics), and whether favorable coverage correlates with financial benefits or contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeking government approval for reporting and reciprocal rewards
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that media outlets seek government approval for reporting and in exchange receive government scheme advertisement contracts and corporate benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence of pre-clearance practices, altered reporting following government feedback, or sudden awarding of government/advertising contracts after positive coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting a personality cult around Narendra Modi
rubrics_metrics.description: Active promotion of Modi as an invincible figure; coverage framing elections as foregone conclusions or emphasizing personal glorification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess frequency and tone of personalistic coverage, hero/folkloric framing, and avoidance of substantive policy critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disproportionate prime-time coverage advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical indicator: during 2019 general election coverage, Modi received a substantially larger share of prime-time news coverage (33.21%) compared with rivals — criticized as providing unfair advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze airtime metrics, focus of prime-time slots, and imbalance between government/leader coverage versus opposition leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowd manipulation and misleading election/exit poll narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of overstated or misleading exit poll reporting and narratives described as 'crowd manipulation' to create impressions (e.g., projecting far larger seat counts for ruling alliance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare media projections with independent polls and final results; look for coordinated optimistic narratives across outlets prior to results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spreading disinformation during communal incidents and crises
rubrics_metrics.description: Involvement in spreading fake news, disinformation, or narratives that inflame communal tensions (e.g., coverage around Bangladesh anti-Hindu riots; communal framing of events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for retractions, independent fact-checks, regulatory actions (e.g., takedown orders), and patterns of communalizing neutral events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amplifying Islamophobia or communal disharmony
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasting or amplifying content that promotes Islamophobia or communal hatred; some programmes were called for takedown and fined by regulatory bodies for such coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence includes regulatory fines/orders (NBDSA actions), repeated use of communal tropes, and demonizing language about minority communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vilifying protesters and misrepresenting social movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Portrayal of protests (e.g., farmers' protests, Shaheen Bagh) unfairly — demonising protesters by labeling them as extremist or delegitimizing their grievances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess framing, labels used, selection of footage, and omission of protesters' perspectives or contextual facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegations leading to boycotts: sycophancy, bias, hate speech, misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition-led boycotts (e.g., INDIA alliance’s boycott of 14 anchors) cited reasons: these journalists/channels are sycophants of the BJP, biased against opposition, promote hate speech and spread misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boycott lists and their justifications can be used as one indicator but should be weighed against denials and concerns about press freedom raised by watchdogs.

rubrics_metrics.name: International/foreign-interference narratives and targeting foreign leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Media amplification that targets foreign leaders or diasporic politics in ways that have been criticized as 'foreign interference' (e.g., Modi-aligned media amplifying narratives against Justin Trudeau).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for coordinated campaigns across outlets, cross-border narrative amplification, and reports from external monitors or foreign governments documenting interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory and reputational consequences as indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of regulatory takedowns, fines, or sustained criticism from press-freedom organizations indicate problematic coverage consistent with 'Godi media' practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NBDSA/other regulatory orders, CPJ/Amnesty/Reporters Committee statements, and documented scandals (e.g., TRP controversies) as evidentiary markers.
